competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move under the trusted duration-1 P&L convention. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

news.headline: Fed’s Williams Currently Sees No Need for Rate Hike in 2027
news.summary: Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said he still sees one more interest-rate hike as appropriate this year, but at the moment doesn’t believe it will be necessary for the central bank to tighten further into 2027.

news.headline: Global Oil Supply Buffer Running 'Scarily Thin,' Aramco CEO Says
news.summary: The oil stockpiles that cushion the world from supply shocks have become scarily thin unless the Strait of Hormuz reopens, according to Aramco's CEO.

news.headline: Euro-Zone Inflation Tops Estimates to Hit Three-Year High
news.summary: Euro-area inflation quickened more than expected to the highest in three years.

news.headline: Iran's Oil Minister Resigns as Exports Dry Up Under US Pressure
news.summary: Iran's oil minister resigned citing personal reasons as the Islamic Republic tries to sustain its oil industry under a tightening US blockade.

news.headline: LNG Trade Through Hormuz Extends Rebound Despite Shipping Risks
news.summary: Shipments of LNG through the Strait of Hormuz extended a rebound that began in September.

news.headline: UK Firms Predict Faster Price Increases After Energy Costs Surge
news.summary: The resurgence in oil and gas prices drove up UK businesses' inflation expectations as firms planned to pass on cost increases.

news.headline: China Oil Comeback Loses Steam as Iran War Drags On
news.summary: A nascent recovery in Chinese oil demand has begun to falter as the Middle East conflict and limited Iranian supply keep crude prices high.

news.headline: Ray Dalio Warns China, Japan May Pull Back From Treasuries
news.summary: Ray Dalio warned that the US Treasury market is vulnerable to a pullback of demand from China and Japan.

news.headline: Man Group Says 5.5% Yields Risk Cracking AI Capex, US Consumer
news.summary: Man Group's Kristina Hooper warned that surging long-end Treasury yields threaten AI capital expenditures and US consumer resilience.

news.headline: Pimco's Stracke Says AI Spending Drove Yields, Not Inflation
news.summary: Surging capital demand from hyperscalers and the AI ecosystem—not inflation expectations—is the primary force pushing real rates and bond yields higher, Pimco's Stracke said.

news.headline: Saudi Aramco’s New China Refinery Venture Gets First Crude Cargo
news.summary: Saudi Aramco and its local partners have received the first crude cargo for their new refining complex in China, bringing the billion-dollar mega plant a step closer to production.

news.headline: Morgan Stanley Expects Renewal of South African Fuel-Tax Relief
news.summary: Morgan Stanley expects South Africa to reinstate fuel-tax relief measures for three months to cushion consumers from surging oil prices in next week’s budget, along with details of a long-awaited rule change.

research_supplement.summary: Overnight trading left risk assets firm while energy and rates stayed the dominant macro story. The S&P 500 held near 7805 with the VIX at 15.21, even as Brent at 105.69 and WTI at 94.14 kept an inflation and term-premium overhang and gold traded around 4177. NY Fed President Williams said one additional hike could still be appropriate this year but argued against needing further tightening into 2027, a message that sits against a March 2027 SOFR strip near 4.52 versus cash SOFR at 3.87. Euro-area inflation printed a three-year high and UK firms flagged faster price increases tied to energy, while Aramco’s CEO warned global oil buffers are dangerously thin amid Iran supply stress and uneven Hormuz flows. Next focus is whether crude and inflation surprises reprice 2027 policy paths and long yields, and whether equity calm persists if oil stays elevated.

vol-convexity.invalidation: This HOLD is wrong if a later freeze shows a markable options structure with premium, implied vol, and strikes whose convex payoff rates and spot cannot express, and last-resort use is then required.
vol-convexity.thesis: This book is flat. The VIX is 15.21 and the S&P is near 7805, and rates and spot already express the oil and policy tape. A volatility clip is not a last-resort case here because this freeze does not name a markable convex payoff that linear rates or spot fail to express. Stay at the zero cash benchmark rather than paying funding on an unmarkable options clip.

deployment_hurdle.benchmark: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 3.87% as of 2026-10-09, charged on shocked-risk capital as the zero-alpha hurdle.

candidate_assessments.rationale: Cash 10-year marks are in hand at NZ 4.98 versus US 5.21, so the spread is markable at minus 23 basis points. A short even carries a running yield pickup, but 23 basis points is not extreme versus the already-wide 2-year gap, and oil near 106 plus a possible late-2026 hike is a fast adverse path for the US long end. Expected edge after that path does not clear official SOFR on shocked-risk capital.

March 2027 SOFR at 4.515 versus cash 3.87 is markable, and Williams arguing against further 2027 tightening is the best directional tell. One more hike this year plus Brent 105.69, thin oil buffers, and euro-area inflation at a three-year high can reprice 2027 SOFR higher. Probability-weighted edge after that tail is too thin for a high preservation hurdle.

CORRA cash 2.28 and March 2027 at 2.905 are markable, so 62 basis points of hikes are already in the contract. Oil strength is Canada-supportive and can justify that path, so neither a new pay nor a new receive has a clean expected edge over official SOFR charged on shocked-risk capital.

deployment_hurdle.chosen_action_rationale: All three markable candidates fail the official SOFR hurdle on their own economics, not because the packet is incomplete. The book is flat and deployment is not forced, so no-trade is the preservation action.

grinder.invalidation: A receive in March 2027 SOFR becomes interesting if energy backs off and any remaining hike is delivered without a 2027 tightening path, leaving 4.515 clearly rich to a one-and-done hold. A NZ-US 10-year short is only worth revisiting if the spread tightens through about minus 10 basis points with stable oil, not on the current minus-23 print.

opportunity_scan.rationale: Markable at minus 23 basis points off 4.98/5.21, but oil and hike risk hit a receive-US / pay-NZ sleeve.
Williams versus 4.515 is the cleanest US tell; oil and a possible late-2026 hike keep the receive from clearing a high hurdle.
62 basis points of hikes already priced; oil can justify the path, so a new pay or receive is not a preservation ticket.
Long-end receive at 5.21 is the wrong side of high oil and a possible additional hike.
Only 20 basis points over 4.60 cash; edge is too small to pay SOFR on shocked capital.

grinder.thesis: Cash is the right seat. The only clean-looking expressions are a 23 basis-point NZ-US 10-year gap and March 2027 SOFR at 4.515 versus 3.87 cash, but both fail a preservation hurdle once Brent near 106, thin oil buffers, and a possible late-2026 hike are treated as live two-way risks. I will not pay official SOFR on shocked capital to own a non-extreme cross-market basis or to receive 2027 SOFR while energy and euro-area inflation are still pushing term premia up. The book stays flat until a markable dislocation has a catalyst that survives an oil shock.

CORRA March 2027 reprices toward the 3.13 entry or through it. A Treasury-led selloff that leaves New Zealand 10s unchanged would also hurt a short NZ-US spread.

portfolio_construction.chosen_actions_rationale: HOLD the 450 million CORRA receive because the residual versus cash is still large and plausible adverse P&L already sizes the ticket. OPEN 80 million short NZ-US 10-year as a singles-and-doubles overlay on a markable first-percentile dislocation: pay New Zealand and receive US, expected mark higher from minus 23 basis points. Eighty million keeps spread adverse P&L in the low single-digit millions and does not fill risk capital for its own sake.

Concentrated Canadian front-end duration, no hedges, and well inside both the shocked-risk cap and the 50 million drawdown stop.

Williams’ pushback on 2027 tightening supports that 2027 strips are the residual, but Canada already has the expression and the size. New Zealand 10s at 4.98 versus Treasuries at 5.21 is a first-percentile cheap-NZ dislocation and is the only overlay worth adding: pay New Zealand and receive US 10s, not more Canadian duration.

swinger.thesis: March 2027 CORRA still prices more than 60 basis points of tightening versus 2.28 cash after the New York Fed lead argued against a 2027 hike campaign. That is the same overpriced Canadian re-tightening this book is already receiving; overnight oil is accepted volatility, not a reason to stand down while the strip remains rich. Shocked risk on the existing line is small versus a plausible remaining fade toward cash, so the aggressive expression is to add to the receive rather than open a second country.
